notes: Seventh sweep (2026-10-31): five runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2) at head 0814e8d with no uncommitted changes; every run has rc 0, a model_id matching its tier, skills_listed 209 and skill_hash 38869366..., so all runs are graded against the current text.

Rule list: the eight rules whose index row names ecto-phoenix, as in 2026-10-23. git diff d04061d -- idiomatic-elixir/ changes one of them, Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call, which is graded against its current text. The six ecto-phoenix.md rules and the directive-order rule are unchanged and graded to the 2026-10-23 standard.

Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call, current text: the sentence that decides every verdict is "Unless a call's result is bound to a name, each of its arguments is a name, a short literal, or a trailing keyword list: a map or struct that would span several lines is built first under a name that says what it is, one field per line, with a blank line between multi-line statements." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md, that rule). Under it the audit maps are named in opus-1 (104-109), haiku-1 (119-124) and sonnet-2 (154-157), and every render(conn, :show, post: post) passes a trailing keyword list. Two other sentences settle edge cases: "A shorter literal that fits its line stays on one line." keeps haiku-2's one-line three-field map at line 118 and sonnet-1's two-field attrs at line 112 clean, and "A call whose result is bound to a name may take its options inline" covers every multi-line from(...) bound to query or unpublished. The more-than-six-elements sentence is not triggered: no literal in any run has more than four elements. 0 of 5 violated, the same as 2026-10-23 under the old text.

Validate input with changesets: haiku-2 is violated. Its changeset (lines 38-42) casts and validates but declares neither foreign_key_constraint/3 nor assoc_constraint/3 for belongs_to :user (line 29), which the rule's sentence "Declare database constraints in the changeset (`unique_constraint/3`, and `foreign_key_constraint/3` or `assoc_constraint/3` for a `belongs_to`) so a violation returns `{:error, changeset}` instead of raising." requires; this is the 2026-10-21 baseline Haiku shape. The other four declare the constraint (opus-1, haiku-1, sonnet-1 assoc_constraint(:user); sonnet-2 foreign_key_constraint(:user_id)). Every run casts only [:title, :body] and sets user_id on the struct.

Keep migrations to schema changes: 0 of 5 (haiku-1 was violated in 2026-10-23). Every migration only adds the column, and every run puts the backfill elsewhere: opus-1, haiku-1 and haiku-2 in a script, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 in a Mix task. haiku-1's script uses the schema (line 148: alias MyApp.Blog.Post; line 152: from p in Post,), which misses the case check but not the rule, since it is not a migration (the 2026-10-22-d standard). haiku-1's script also calls Repo.update_all(query) at line 156; Ecto's Repo defines update_all(queryable, updates, opts \\ []), so that call has no matching arity and fails when the script runs. No rule covers this; it is recorded in the summary only.

The other five listed rules: 0 of 5 violated. All five publish with Repo.transact/2 and a two-step with; every listing preloads the author (all five now by preload, none by join); every controller shows via Blog.get_post!/1 over Repo.get!/2; directive order is clean in every module, including the two Mix tasks (@shortdoc, @moduledoc, then use, import, alias).

Changed rules outside the list, checked as other_violations: no run has a case, cond, receive or with ... else, so the renamed `->` rule has no clause to judge; every with has two steps, so the one-step and tail-call sentences do not apply; no pipeline sits on one line (haiku-2 did in 2026-10-23); no run uses a capture; no do: body holds a fn; the nested calls Repo.update(Post.publish_changeset(post)) (opus-1 line 94) and Repo.update(Post.publish_changeset(post, published_at)) (haiku-1 line 111) are one expression each, which the new Readability rules keep as written. The multi-clause publish_post/1 in sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 select on published_at with a literal or a struct pattern and bind only post. 0 of 5 runs have an other_violation. Assumption and reason comments (opus-1 74, 101-102, 129-145, 166; haiku-1 1-10, 144-145; haiku-2 1-7, 139-143; sonnet-1 109-110; sonnet-2 1-3, 39) say what the code cannot show and are not counted.

format_ok: result.json reports false for all five because plain mix format adds parentheses to the Ecto and Phoenix DSL calls. As before, the grader recomputed it with Code.format_string!/2 and the DSL calls (field, belongs_to, timestamps, add, from and the rest) in locals_without_parens: all five pass. Nothing compiles because Phoenix and Ecto are not installed.

Transcripts: every run read SKILL.md and references/ecto-phoenix.md and wrote blog.ex in one Write call with no later edit. opus-1 then checked the file with Code.format_string!/2 and DSL locals_without_parens (result: matches formatter: true) after a mix format attempt failed. sonnet-2 ran mix format --check-formatted, which failed only on the DSL parentheses, and said so in its reply. sonnet-1's format command was blocked by the sandbox and its reply says it did not format. haiku-1 ran one cat of SKILL.md; haiku-2 ran no command.
